about: Frames of the two controlled experiments of the paper (main text, section 'Application'; settings in supplement S4): the view-angle sweep (block view_sweep, 17 frames) and the illumination sweep (block light_sweep, 456 frames). Each row gives the scene (configuration, seed, relief a and H, random fault count), the fracture parameters, the sun direction, the render settings and the camera shot (metres, east-north-up), as in frames.json. scene_options and frame_options are the options of `fracgen scene CONFIG ...` and `fracgen frame SCENE ...` that generate the frame (add --out and, for rendering, --device OPTIX; with `--out FRAMES --name FRAME` the frame is written to FRAMES/FRAME, where the scripts in analysis/ look for it by its identifier); run `fracgen cameras SCENE` between the two. Both scenes are scenes of the paper's formal label set (frames.json: 26120001 is the scene of frame a0077, 26130000 that of frame a0044 and of the end-to-end example). camera_slot is the plan camera of the frame; it is empty for the user-defined cameras of the view-angle sweep, which are given with --position, --target and --focal-mm and replace the plan camera of the slot named by --camera in frame_options. The columns not described under 'columns' are those of frames.json.

columns.frame: Identifier of the frame. Sweep and repeat rows of the illumination sweep are named CASE_aAAAeEEsS: sun azimuth AAA and elevation EE in degrees, render seed S. View-angle sweep: vs_f (flat outcrop) or vs_s (standalone outcrop), bNN the off-nadir angle, then z (nadir), p (across strike) or a (along strike).
columns.role: view_sweep: sweep. light_sweep: base = the frame of a case generated with the whole chain (geometry, rendering, labels) under the light of the paper frame of its viewpoint; sweep = one of the 72 sun directions of a case; repeat = a sun direction rendered again with render seed 1; full_chain = a sun direction of the sweep generated independently with the whole chain.
columns.case: view_sweep: vs_f (target point on the flat outcrop) or vs_s (target point on the standalone outcrop). light_sweep: the viewpoint and shape-parameter case, ls_v1b055 (V1 baseline: mean opening 5.5 cm, depth 0.175 m), ls_v1w030 and ls_v1w080 (mean opening 3 and 8 cm), ls_v1d010 and ls_v1d025 (depth 0.10 and 0.25 m), ls_v2b055 (V2 baseline).
columns.viewpoint: light_sweep: V1 = camera slot 0 of the flat outcrop 26120001 (6.40 mm/px), V2 = camera slot 1 of the standalone outcrop 26130000 (4.07 mm/px). Empty for the view-angle sweep.
columns.camera_slot: Camera slot of `fracgen frame` whose plan camera has this shot; empty (null) for a user-defined camera.
columns.beta_deg: view_sweep: off-nadir angle (angle between the zenith and the target-to-camera direction), degrees.
columns.camera_azimuth_deg: view_sweep: horizontal azimuth A of the camera seen from the target, degrees clockwise from north (empty for the nadir view).
columns.azimuth_kind: view_sweep: nadir, across strike (A perpendicular to the strike of the target fracture) or along strike.

view_sweep.rule: Camera position = target + distance x (sin(b) sin(A), sin(b) cos(A), cos(b)) in east, north, up, with the off-nadir angle b = 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 degrees and the camera azimuth A across or along the strike of the target fracture, each on the side nearer to the camera azimuth of the plan camera. Target point and distance are those of the plan camera of the slot (plan.json: shot.target_enu_m and shot.position_enu_m); the strike is its light_reference.azimuth_deg. Sun elevation 40 degrees, sun azimuth A + 30 degrees (for the nadir view, A of the across-strike group). Baseline fracture parameters, 1024 px, 1024 samples, render seed 0, focal length 35 mm.
view_sweep.checks: The 17 frames passed the checks of checks.json.
view_sweep.time: Each frame was generated with the whole chain: 8 to 33 minutes per frame on the tested machine with up to four frames running at a time.

not_generated.reason: The camera position lies inside the rock body: the rock surface is 2.3 m above it, and the first rock surface along the optical axis is met from behind. `fracgen frame` stops with an error in the cavity construction (exit status 1), and there is no such viewpoint.

light_sweep.rule: Per case, 72 sun directions: azimuth 0 to 345 degrees in steps of 15 degrees at elevations 20, 40 and 60 degrees, 1024 samples, render seed 0. The two baseline cases have 6 repeats with render seed 1: (azimuth, elevation) = (0, 40), (90, 40), (180, 40), (270, 40), (45, 20), (45, 60). The full_chain frames are the sun directions (90, 20), (210, 40) and (330, 60) at each viewpoint.
light_sweep.base_frames: The base frames ls_v1b055 and ls_v2b055 have the options of the paper frames a0077 and a0044 (frames.json). Their label layers were bit-identical to those of the paper frames, and so were depth, material index and region mask of the render; the PNG images differed by one 8-bit level in 31 and 14 of 3,145,728 values. These two base frames and their sweep and repeat rows carry the cavity depth as written for the paper frames (0.17500000000000002 m); the other rows with the baseline depth were run with 0.175 m.
light_sweep.how_rendered: In the original runs the sweep and repeat frames of a case were rendered on the cut geometry of its base frame: only the sun direction and the render seed of the base frame's render specification were changed (about 6 s per image, 49 minutes for the 444 images; analysis/light_sweep.py renders the sweep of a case in this way from its base frame), and the windows of the contrast test stored with the base frame's labels (trace_labels/windows.json with the pixel memberships of window_pixels.npz) were used for every sun direction. Rendered this way under its own light, each base frame was reproduced with identical depth, material index and region mask and with one 8-bit level of difference in at most 32 of 3,145,728 PNG values. The frame_options of a sweep or repeat row generate the frame with the whole chain instead, which builds the geometry again from the scene, the camera and the fracture parameters (they do not depend on the light) and takes about as long as the base frame (10 to 17 minutes). The two routes were compared on the 6 full_chain frames: the window sets were identical (483 windows at V1, 172 at V2), depth, material index and region mask of the two renders were identical, the PNG images differed by one 8-bit level in 13 to 67 values, the brightness difference between ring and band of a window differed by at most 0.014 grey levels and every window was classified identically.
light_sweep.checks: The 6 base frames and the 6 full_chain frames passed the checks of checks.json.

experiments.scenes: Flat outcrop 26120001 and standalone outcrop 26130000, both without faults. In the original runs the standalone scene was the scene of the end-to-end example (examples/minimal/scene_config.json, whose content equals configs/scenes/standalone_outcrop.json).
